paragraphs: I'm applying for the Infrastructure Investment Associate role on the DWS infrastructure debt team in New York. I'm an MBA Finance (STEM) candidate at Fordham Gabelli, and before that I worked at JPMorgan Asset Management, Lenovo and Thomson Reuters. What draws me to the team is the mix of renewables, utilities, transportation and digital infrastructure. Data center and power financing is the area I most want to build a career in, and private debt is where a lot of that capital comes from.

The closest work I've done is an MBA project modeling a 6-project, 35.4 MW Illinois solar portfolio. I built project and portfolio models covering capital structure, DSCR, NPV and levered IRR under post-ITC scenarios, compared senior debt, sustainability-linked loan and green loan plus ABS structures, and recommended a phased green loan + ABS approach that reduced sponsor equity by $11.1M in the model and improved levered IRR from 8.58% to 9.79%. At Lenovo I built forecasts and scenario analyses on capital allocation that improved capital efficiency by 15%.

I want to be upfront that my modeling experience comes from MBA coursework and projects, and I haven't worked in leveraged finance, so I'd be learning execution on the job. What I can bring from day one is careful modeling, comfort with debt metrics like DSCR, and the habit of checking a number before it goes into a committee memo or a portfolio report. I'd welcome the chance to talk.
